A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MARIE and retain matching core methods and experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SMAC evaluations, ablations, prediction-error measurements, and attention analyses, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original SMAC results and additional MAMujoco, SMACv2, and controlled comparison experiments in Appendix E.

M1.justification: v1 uses categorical reward prediction with HL-Gauss targets, with an L1 exception documented for 3s_vs_5z. v2 specifies smooth L1 reward prediction generally and removes the categorical formulation. The VQ-VAE, shared Transformer, Perceiver, and actor-critic procedure remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained 13 SMAC scenarios, v2 evaluates three continuous-control MAMujoco configurations and three SMACv2 scenarios with greater stochasticity and partial observability (Appendices E.1–E.2). These substantially broaden the tested domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates HAPPO, adapts MAMBA for continuous-action comparisons, and tests self-attention aggregation against Perceiver aggregation. The original SMAC comparator set remains. The IRIS variants in Appendix E.4 correspond to existing centralized and no-aggregation ablations, rather than newly added methods.

E3.justification: Added protocols include MAMujoco evaluation up to two million steps, with MAMBA limited to one million on Walker2d, and SMACv2 evaluation over 200,000 steps. New controls vary epsilon-annealing time and imagination horizon and match aggregation depth. The original SMAC budgets and ten-game evaluations are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds epsilon-annealing sensitivity, imagination-horizon comparisons, and aggregation performance/FLOPs analyses (Appendices E.3, E.5–E.6). v1's reward-loss ablation in Figure 10 is removed. The earlier centralization, aggregation-removal, tokenizer, prediction-error, and attention analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 reports four-seed medians and standard deviations. v2 changes Table 1 to means and adds stratified-bootstrap confidence intervals for aggregate mean, median, and interquartile mean, plus probability-of-improvement reporting (Figures 3 and 14). The main experiment still uses four seeds; no increase is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises scores and rankings: on MMM, MARIE/QPLEX change from 25.0/88.4 as medians to 87.6/69.3 as means, reversing their reported ranking. These are not directly comparable performance gains. New benchmark and sensitivity results substantially expand the findings, including MARIE leading in two of three MAMujoco configurations.

T1.justification: The categorical reward-distribution definition and Gaussian histogram-label construction in v1's Equation 6 and Appendix B are removed. The Dec-POMDP formulation and remaining dynamics and policy-learning mathematics are retained, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and fourth introductory contribution extend the empirical effectiveness claim from SMAC to SMAC and MAMujoco. The central novelty claims about a Transformer-based multi-agent world model combining decentralized dynamics with centralized Perceiver aggregation remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications about model capacity partly explaining performance differences, the limitations of four seeds, and recurrent features or oracle-state access explaining HalfCheetah performance gaps. It also interprets the new sensitivity analyses and removes v1's explanation of poor MMM performance through short-term cooperation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a MARIE code-access link, explicit action-mask-head documentation, 256-bin continuous-action encoding, model-size information, and training-time/GPU-memory estimates. Existing architecture specifications, hardware disclosures, SMAC hyperparameters, and pseudocode largely persist. The mask-head description alone does not establish a newly introduced component.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused discussion and citations concerning CoDreamer/GATv2, SMACv2, and statistical evaluation, and explicitly positions existing ablations as IRIS adaptations. The reward-distribution references to Farebrother and Imani–White are removed. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites motivation and complexity explanations, separates experimental setup from main results, and reorganizes the appendices. Affiliations, citation style, and the conclusion heading change. Much of the original method, ablation, and analysis prose remains, so this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: New statistical plots, benchmark curves, and sensitivity/resource tables substantially expand the visual presentation. Table 1 gains model-size information and colored highlighting; retained figures receive revised captions and placement within the TMLR layout. Existing ablation variants are redisplayed together as IRIS comparisons, while the reward-loss plot disappears.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's SMAC-only evidence through continuous-control and stochastic SMACv2 evaluations, controlled sensitivity comparisons, and bootstrap uncertainty analyses. Code and computational-cost disclosures, together with explicit capacity and statistical limitations, improve reproducibility and interpretation. Four-seed uncertainty and unequal Walker2d comparison budgets still limit conclusions, but the broader validation and transparency provide a substantial overall gain.
